semantic_generation_oracle_01.inputPolicyFinding: Postgres codebase_chunk_index.embedding_model literally reads 'embeddinggemma:latest:eg-task-prefix-v1' for every row tested -- appearing to contradict embedding-contract-768.ts's doc comment that the whole corpus was embedded PROMPT_REVISION_UNPROMPTED (raw text, no formatEmbeddingGemmaInput() prefix). Tested empirically rather than trusting either the field or the comment: raw/unprompted input reproduces generation B's stored vector far more closely (cosine 0.998-0.99998) than formatEmbeddingGemmaInput('document', text) does (cosine 0.95-0.97). CONCLUSION: the code comment is empirically correct; the embedding_model metadata field's 'eg-task-prefix-v1' suffix is itself stale/mislabeled -- another case of a self-declared payload label not matching physical reality, consistent with every other finding in this investigation chain.

semantic_generation_oracle_01.conclusion: DECISIVE for the 2 genuinely-diverged test cases: generation B's stored vector matches a fresh embedding of the file's CURRENT content, computed via the actual code-declared canonical executor, at cosine >=0.998. Generation C1's stored vector does NOT match (cosine 0.46-0.68, no better than unrelated content) despite C1 self-declaring representation_id='semantic_768' -- the code-canonical LABEL -- while B self-declares the non-canonical-sounding 'embeddinggemma_768_native_v1'. This reverses the label-based hypothesis from the prior turn: a correct-looking representation_id string is not evidence of a correct vector. B is the generation whose vectors are actually current and executor-verified; C1's label is more 'correct' but its data is stale or wrong. Sample size is small (2 discriminating cases) -- reported as decisive for what was tested, not yet generalized to the full 7,711 population without a larger run.
semantic_generation_oracle_01.knownBlocker: The embed server's configured ubatch size (128, per the dev:gpu startup log) rejects inputs over ~128 tokens with HTTP 500 'input too large to process' -- this is the SAME bug already diagnosed in memory/SESSION-201-EG-GGUF-PROOF-GATES-0-2.md (EMBED_UBATCH_SIZE=128 default; -ub silently capped by -b, both need to reach EMBED_CTX=2048). Reproduced live, not fixed here (no infra restart performed) -- scaled the oracle up by filtering to short-content chunks only, staying inside the existing config rather than changing it.

semantic_generation_oracle_01_scaled.purpose: Generalize the n=2 SEMANTIC-GENERATION-ORACLE-01 result across a larger bounded sample, without restarting the embed server (stayed under its existing ubatch=128 limit by filtering to short-content chunks, content.length<=400 chars as a conservative token-count proxy).

semantic_generation_oracle_01_scaled.conclusion: GENERALIZED AND STRENGTHENED. Across 56 cases where B and C1 actually carry different vectors, the fresh canonical-executor embedding of current file content matched B in 56/56 (100%) and never matched C1 better. The remaining 3 were non-discriminating (B and C1 happened to be the identical vector, both matched fresh equally -- same pattern as the earlier n=1 outlier, now understood as a small minority case, not a counterexample). Zero cases favored C1. This is no longer a 2-example spot check: generation B (embeddinggemma_768_native_v1-labeled) is the generation with current, executor-verified vectors; generation C1 (semantic_768-labeled) carries stale or wrong vectors in every discriminating case sampled, despite its more code-canonical-sounding label.

trace_mcp_startup_01.status: DIAGNOSED, no code change made -- self-resolved before intervention needed
trace_mcp_startup_01.mechanism: scripts/ensure-mcp-server.mjs checks /health (dependencies.mcp===true) THEN separately calls tools/list and requires 6 hardcoded REQUIRED_TOOLS names to all be present (kag.record_agent_run, kag.ingest_memory_directory, runtime.simdjson_status, runtime.sse_probe, hypergraph.explain_activation, trace.kag_search). If health passes but any required tool is missing, it logs 'healthy but missing required tools' and restarts the listener.
trace_mcp_startup_01.liveCheck: Queried :8788/health (ok, dependencies.mcp=true) and POST :8788/mcp tools/list directly after dev:gpu settled: 175 tools returned, all 6 REQUIRED_TOOLS present, missingToolNames=[]. trace.kag_search and kb.trace_search both present.
trace_mcp_startup_01.rootCause: NOT an obsolete-tool-name / protocol-mismatch problem -- all 6 required names are real, current, live tool names once the server fully starts. This was a startup-ordering RACE: /health flips to healthy before the full 175-tool catalog finishes registering (likely async registry loading), so a tools/list call issued in that narrow window returns a partial catalog. ensure-mcp-server's own detect-and-restart logic caught exactly this and self-corrected by restarting the listener -- which is why the state is now fully healthy with zero missing tools.
trace_mcp_startup_01.actionTaken: None -- diagnosed only, per the instruction not to repeatedly restart the listener until the reason is known. The reason is now known (a real, transient startup race, not a config/protocol defect) and the system already self-healed. No code fix applied; a future hardening could have /health itself report tool-catalog readiness so ensure-mcp-server doesn't need a second racy check, but that's a design choice, not an active bug to patch now.

emb3a_prior_audit_read_in_full.whyBlocked_notAWriterBug: The blocker is UPSTREAM, not in the Qdrant writer. atlas_packets.workspace_revision: populated for 0/61,660 rows. atlas_packets.source_representation_id: populated for 1/61,660 rows. atlas_packets.representation_revision: 1/61,660. atlas_packets.encoder_revision: 1/61,660. atlas_symbol_versions (the table that SHOULD own symbol_version_id/workspace_revision/source_revision): does not exist in this schema at all (exists:false). The writer (backfill-qdrant-768-v2-uuid.mjs) can't populate fields Postgres itself doesn't have data for -- this is a pre-existing, already-documented Postgres data-completeness gap, confirmed here, not introduced or discovered by this session's own investigation.
emb3a_prior_audit_read_in_full.consequenceForThisInvestigation: This session independently PROVED something the prior audit did not check: D's VECTOR content is correct (matches B, matches fresh embeddings, 40/40). Combined, the full picture is: D has correct vectors + correct identity/source linkage, but near-total absence of revision/representation lineage metadata -- not because anyone wrote it wrong, but because the Postgres columns it should read from are themselves unpopulated. A QDRANT_PROJECTION_OWNERSHIP freeze that also implies 'lineage-complete' would be premature even now that vector-correctness is proven. Repointing atlas_packets/bridge at B or D would fix the vector-correctness problem this session found, but would not by itself fix the separate, larger, upstream lineage-population gap this prior audit already found and this session did not attempt to address.

whatThisInvestigationEstablished_newThis: The 143-row 'dual-live numeric+UUID' framing undersold the scope: 10,302 rows carry a legacy numeric qdrant_id, and atlas_packets/bridge reference a third, distinct generation (C) for 7,773+55 of them -- not the numeric or UUID generation directly.

Generation C is not monolithic: a majority (C1, ~86% sampled) self-labels representation_id=semantic_768 (the code-canonical string); a minority (C2, ~14%) has an unexplained UUID-valued representation_id; a trace contaminant matches generation B exactly.

Vector-level oracle (real code-traced :8081 canonical executor, not assumed): generation B and generation D (codebase_chunks_768_v2) carry the IDENTICAL, current, correct vector in 40/40 tested cases. Generation C1 -- despite the more code-canonical-sounding label -- does not match in 39/40.

The live default search reader (qdrant-search.ts) queries codebase_chunks_768 (contains B, C1, and the rest), not _768_v2, and its atlas_enriched filter does not exclude C1 -- so this is a live retrieval-quality risk, not just dormant metadata.
TRACE MCP's 'missing required tools' warning was a real but transient startup race, not a defect -- diagnosed, not patched, since it self-resolved.
whatWasAlreadyKnownBeforeThisSession_con: codebase_chunks_768 vs _768_v2 non-dedup was already flagged in root CLAUDE.md.

D's writer (backfill-qdrant-768-v2-uuid.mjs) and D's lineage-field gaps were already fully documented in emb3a-qdrant-lineage-audit.json (2026-08-22) -- found late in this investigation via grep for a specific revision string, not checked first as the repo's own Duplication Prevention rule recommends.
final_synthesis.recommendation: Do not proceed to reconciliation or a QDRANT_PROJECTION_OWNERSHIP freeze yet. Vector-correctness (this session's contribution) and lineage-completeness (the prior EMB3A audit's finding) are two separate, both-necessary conditions, and only the first is now well-evidenced. Populating atlas_packets.workspace_revision/representation_revision/encoder_revision/source_representation_id (currently ~0% populated across 61,660 rows) and resolving whether atlas_symbol_versions needs to be created are prerequisites larger than this investigation's read-only scope -- a separate, deliberate piece of work, not a natural continuation of this census.
